newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Italian minister says troops in Albania seek peace.
newsitem.headline: Italian minister says troops in Albania seek peace.

text.p: Italian Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta said a multinational force that arrived in Albania on Tuesday would help restore peace in a nation racked by weeks of anarchy.

Speaking in the windswept western port city of Durres after more than 1,000 Italian, French and Spanish troops landed, Andreatta said the soldiers were armed with weapons they hoped they would not have to use.
"We are here to help the Albanian people at a time of national difficulty and I hope that this will be understood by all Albanians," Andreatta told the troops in Durres.
"We hope that in three months, or a few months more, that everyone will return home together, leaving behind them an Albanian people proud of its destiny and proud of its future."

The Italian-led eight-nation force reached Albania on Tuesday in a well-orchestrated show of military force. French, Italian and Spanish troops came on shore in Durres while Italian paratroopers landed at Tirana airport 40 km (25 miles) east.
Greece, Turkey, Austria, Denmark and Romania are also contributing soldiers to the mission.
"The soldiers that have come to Durres are all carrying arms but they have a profound sense of humanity," Andreatta said. "They know they are ambassadors of civility and humanity."

He warned there were no easy solutions to the problems in Albania, where nearly 300 people have been killed during a spasm of lawlessness following the collapse of fraudulent get-rich-quick investment schemes earlier this year.
"The principal difficulty facing the mission is the very reason why we have come to Albania," said the defence minister.

"It is certainly a risk to work in an environment of anarchy. There can be tensions and incidents. We are here precisely to help reconciliation come about. The presence of military forces could lead people in hot spots of violence to realise the futility of that violence."

Italy is sending 2,500 troops to Albania, Europe's poorest nation. A total of 6,000 troops are expected to arrive within three weeks and will stay for at least three months. They may stay for another three months if needed.
Andreatta attended a ceremony earlier on Tuesday at the southeast Italian port of Brindisi where he handed the mission's flag to the commander of the operation of the ground, General Luigi Forlani.
"The arms that you carry and which, if necessary, you will use, are at the service of the aims and objectives which Europe and the United Nations have clearly indicated," Andreatta said.

He said Italy and Europe were committed to helping Albania "find unity again and strengthen its democratic system which has shown great fragility in these first years following the end of totalitarianism."
